x: Myna Myna is a workbench for data and machine learning, written in Crow over Magpie . It holds everything a team does with data in one place: the catalog of tables; queries, asked as forms, and dashboards made of them; notebooks of Crow cells; experiments and models, as MLflow keeps them; the jobs that run all of it on a schedule. Every piece of its state is a Magpie log in one folder, the workspace. The notebooks' tables sit beside Myna's own records. There is no second database, no Python and no JavaScript framework: the pages are Crow views, served by Crow, in both of its modes. What it is made of Part Written in Kept in The pages Crow views ( use ui ) nothing: they are derived from the logs Notebooks and their runs Crow, run by the crow on the PATH _notebooks , _runs Queries and dashboards Magpie's reading verbs _queries , _dashboards , _tiles Experiments and models Crow, answering MLflow's own client _ml_* logs and .mlartifacts/ The scheduler a Crow program of its own _schedules , _runs Reading this book Part I walks through the workbench, one page at a time. Part II is experiments and models: what MLflow's parts are, how Myna holds them, and how a notebook, the pages and MLflow's own client reach them. Part III is the reference: tests, the code, and what is not built. The name The myna is the clever talking bird of every Indian town. The mark is Crow's face between two amber quotation marks, "(o.o)" : the one that talks. Status Every page but the model to ask is built, and that page says so. Myna's source is at github.com/agncrow/myna , under the Business Source License 1.1 ( Licensing ).

Installing and Running Myna Myna needs Crow 0.8.2 or later: building Myna found 31 bugs in Crow, and 0.8.2 is the release that fixes them. Crow installs in one line, fetching a C toolchain and Rust if they are missing: curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/agncrow/crow/main/install.sh | bash the Crow Book says more. Then get Myna, install Magpie (its one dependency, pinned by crow.lock ) and start it: git clone https://github.com/agncrow/myna cd myna crow install crow run main.co crow run main.co builds the compiled program and serves it on http://localhost:3800 . The first build takes a few minutes; an edit rebuilds in seconds. crow run -i main.co interprets it instead, with no build. It still reads the whole program before it serves: from a fresh clone that took 138 seconds on the Mac Studio it was timed on. Every page works the same way in both modes, but the interpreter derives each open page again from the logs on every refresh. Once a few sessions are open, a click on an Experiments page took 9 to 17 seconds interpreted, against under 0.1 seconds compiled. These are times seen while checking the pages in a browser, not a benchmark. Use the compiled program for real work, and the interpreter for a quick look. The workspace folder Myna keeps everything in myna_data/ beside the program. MYNA_DATA names another folder: MYNA_DATA=my_workspace crow run main.co The folder must lie inside Myna's checkout, where the programs a notebook runs find crow_modules/ . Sample data tests/mlflow/house_prices.co trains, registers, evaluates and serves a small model, so the Experiments and Models pages have something to show: crow run -i tests/mlflow/house_prices.co It adds an experiment and a model to the workspace and deletes nothing. Put MYNA_DATA=… in front of both commands to keep the sample out of your own workspace.

Notebooks Since 2026-11-07 the notebooks live on the Code page ( / ), the project's files in a tree with the notebooks first: a notebook is a file, notebooks/<name>.co , its cells marked by --- %% lines, and any .co file opens as cells or as text. The rest of this chapter holds: cells, runs, outputs, schedules and History are as described, with versions now the file's commits, made from the Git drawer. The Notebooks page ( / ) lists the workspace's notebooks. A notebook is a list of cells of Crow. Running a notebook A run takes the cells top to bottom as one program , run by the crow on the PATH in the workspace's folder. So a name one cell sets is there in the next, and a table a cell writes is a Magpie log beside the others, which the Catalog then shows. Under each cell are its output, its status and how long it took: A stop or a refusal is shown under the cell it names, by the cell's own line, and the cells after it are skipped. A run that takes longer than the workspace allows (60 seconds unless Settings says otherwise) is stopped. The side panel names the variables the cells left and the tables they read and write. Keys The cell being edited is drawn by Lory's editor (since 2026-11-07): line numbers, Crow coloured, the caret placed by a press, the wheel scrolling by the pixel, a paste going in as typed text. Key Does Ctrl+Enter Save, then run the cells down to this one Ctrl+Shift+Enter Save, then run every cell Ctrl+S Save Tab, Shift+Tab Indent to the next four spaces, take four back Enter A new line, indented as the one it came from Home The line's first character, then its start Escape Cancel an edit (Cmd stands for Ctrl on a Mac.) History Every save is a version, and every run is kept with its output. History lists both: it opens a run's output, and restores a version. A schedule A notebook can run on a schedule, which the scheduler keeps (see Jobs and the Scheduler ). Each scheduled run is recorded as the schedule's, and the Jobs page lists it. Logging experiments A cell that trains a model logs into Experiments with a few calls: see Logging from a Notebook .

Query and the Catalog The Catalog The Catalog ( /catalog ) lists the workspace's tables, each a Magpie log, with their columns and their latest rows. Query this table opens the Query page on it. Query The Query page ( /query ) asks one of Magpie's reading verbs of a table, as a form: Latest rows : the columns named, or all. A summary : grouped by columns, a column reduced by sum, count, mean, min, max, std, var, first or last, over the rows a predicate admits. A search of a text column: words, phrases, prefixes ( kit* ) and fuzzy words ( kitchn~ ). The answer is a table and, for a summary, bars. A query is saved by name in the workspace's _queries log and opened again from the list. Open as notebook writes it as the first cell of a new notebook, so a question asked as a form can grow into a program. Pin to puts it on a dashboard.

Dashboards A dashboard ( /dashboards ) sets saved queries side by side as tiles. Each tile is drawn as bars, a number or a table. A query is added from the dashboard, or pinned from the Query page. Tiles are moved and removed in place. Refresh now asks every tile's query again. A dashboard given an interval (1 min, 15 min, 1 h or 1 d) is refreshed by the scheduler. Each tile's answer is kept as a Parquet file under .tiles/ , so a dashboard opens without asking its queries again. The dashboards are kept in the _dashboards log, their tiles in _tiles .

Jobs and the Scheduler The Jobs page ( /jobs ) shows the scheduler, the schedules and every run. The scheduler A notebook's schedule is kept in the workspace ( _schedules ), and the scheduler runs it. The Jobs page starts the scheduler as a process of its own: crow run -i scheduler.co 3800 Every fifteen seconds it runs the notebooks that are due, and records each run as the schedule's. It also refreshes the dashboards that are due. It ends when the page asks it to, or when the page has not answered for three rounds. crow run scheduler.co runs it without a page, until the file myna_data/_scheduler.stop is written.

The Workspace and Settings The workspace Code is files in a project; data is logs in Magpie. Myna's own folder, myna_data/ unless MYNA_DATA names another, holds the workspace's records and the scratch project, the one worked in while no project is open: In Myna's folder Holds _users , _grants who may sign in, and their grants on projects _projects the projects opened (Projects) scratch/ the scratch project: a crowfile , myna.json , notebooks/ , queries/ , data/ In a project Holds notebooks/<name>.co a notebook: a Crow program, its cells marked by --- %% lines queries/<name>.json a saved query myna.json the dashboards and their tiles, the schedules, the settings data/_runs every run and its output data/_answers , data/.tiles/ each tile's last refresh and its kept answer data/_ml_* experiments and models ( how ) data/<any other name> a table a program or a notebook wrote A log's change is a new row, and a read takes the latest row per key, so nothing is edited in place and the history of every record is kept. A file's history is git's. Settings The Settings page ( /settings ) holds the workspace's name, and how long a run may take before it is stopped (60 seconds unless set). An admin changes them. Users and access A workspace with no users is one person's own: the reader is the account Myna runs as, an admin, and no page asks for a sign-in. The Users page ( /users ) adds the first user — an admin, whatever role was asked — and signs you in as them; from then on every page asks for a sign-in, and a page draws nothing else until one is given. A user has a role: an admin does everything, a member what their grants allow. The Access page ( /access ) gives a member a grant on a project: a viewer reads it, an editor reads and writes, an owner grants too. A reader with no grant on the open project is told so, and a reader without an editor's grant changes nothing: the handlers that write refuse them. Passwords are kept as Crow's password hash (Argon2id), never as themselves, and the sign-in is Crow's signed cookie, good for thirty days or until Sign out. Where this is going — projects as apps built on Myna, a server many people share — is docs/platform.md . Search The search in the top bar finds notebooks and tables by name.

t: MLflow's Parts, and How Myna Holds Them
x: MLflow's Parts, and How Myna Holds Them Myna keeps the record of machine-learning work the way MLflow does: the experiments, the runs inside them, what each run was given and what it scored, the files it made, the models kept from it, and how a kept model is called. All of it is written in Crow. Every record is a row of a Magpie log in the workspace, beside the notebooks' tables. There is no second database and no Python. MLflow's parts, from the start Part The question it answers What it holds Experiment Which piece of work is this? A name, an id, tags Run What happened in one attempt? Start and end, a status, the user, the source, a parent run Params What settings did the attempt use? Key and value, set once Metrics How well did it do, step by step? Key, value, step and time; every value kept, so a curve can be drawn Tags What else is worth saying? Key and value on runs, experiments, models and versions Datasets What data was it given? Name, digest, source, schema, and its use (train, eval) Artifacts What files did it make? A folder per run Logged model Which model came out of the run? An id, its files, its metrics, the run Registered model Which model is kept, and which version is live? A name, numbered versions, aliases ( champion ), stages, tags Prompt Which prompt text is in use? Versioned text with {{variables}} , kept as a registered model Trace What did an LLM application do on one request? A tree of spans with inputs, outputs and times, and feedback Serving How is the model called? An HTTP endpoint answering predictions Evaluation Is the model good enough? Standard scores, logged to a run A notebook logs into a run as it trains. The pages then compare runs, pick the best, register it, and try it. How Myna holds it A change is a new row. A read takes the latest row per key ( magpie.latest ). So a delete is a row whose stage is deleted , a restore is another row, history is never rewritten, and two writers never edit one row in place. Log One row per Kept _ml_experiments experiment change the latest per id _ml_runs run change the latest per id _ml_params param the first per run and key (a param never changes) _ml_metrics metric value logged every value _ml_latest run and metric the greatest step, then time, then value _ml_tags tag set or deleted the latest per entity, id, version and key _ml_inputs dataset given to a run the latest per run, digest and use _ml_logged , _ml_outputs logged model, and the run that made it the latest _ml_models , _ml_versions , _ml_aliases registry change the latest per name, version, alias _ml_traces trace the latest per trace; spans in the trace's files Files live in .mlartifacts/<experiment>/<run>/artifacts/ and .mlartifacts/<experiment>/models/<model id>/artifacts/ in the workspace, MLflow's own layout, so MLflow's client reads and writes them in place.

The Experiments and Models Pages The sidebar has Experiments and Models . Prompts and traces are tabs inside those two. Every page is drawn with what Myna's other pages use: the workbench frame, bordered cards, the tab strip from Dashboards, primary buttons, and a modal for every create or rename. Experiments ( /experiments ): the experiments on the left, the chosen one's runs on the right. The Runs tab is a table: name, created, duration, source, status, the latest metrics and the params. Child runs sit under their parent at any sort. You can filter with MLflow's search grammar ( metrics.rmse < 6000 and params.lr = '0.3' ), sort by any column, show deleted runs and restore them, pick runs, delete them, compare them, or chart them. New and Rename open modals. The Models tab lists the logged models. The Traces tab lists the traces. Opening one shows its spans as a tree, each with a time bar, and the picked span's inputs and outputs. Feedback (thumbs up or down) is written on the trace. The Charts tab draws one chart per metric across the picked runs, with step, time or elapsed time on x. Run ( /runs/:run_id ): three tabs. Overview : status, times, user, source, parent, the description (editable), params, latest metrics, tags, datasets and the models it logged. Metrics : one line chart per metric. Artifacts : the folder tree, with a text file opened beside it (the first 64 kB). Compare ( /compare?runs=a,b,c ): params and metrics side by side, with ● marking every row whose values differ. There is a scatter of any two values (x and y chosen from the lists), and one chart per metric with a line per run. Models ( /models ): the registered models (name, latest version, aliases, description), filtered by name, and a Prompts tab. New opens a modal. Model ( /models/:model_name ): the description (editable), the versions as a table (version, aliases, stage, source run, created), and a version opened in a panel. The panel shows the version's run, its MLmodel , and whether it can be served. You can set or drop aliases, move the stage, and delete the version. Its Try it box takes MLflow's input as JSON and shows the prediction the served model answers. A prompt's version shows its text with the {{variables}} , and a form fills them. The charts are SVG drawn in Crow ( myna/charts.co ). They sort by x, fit y to the data with 5% room at each end, and leave a gap at a NaN.

Logging from a Notebook A cell like this one makes a run, records what it was given and how it did, and ends it. The run then shows on the Experiments page: use myna.tracking tracking.ready[] run = tracking.start_run['house-prices', 'linear-lr0.1'] p = tracking.log_params[run, map[lr = '0.1', epochs = '60']] for step in range[60] m = tracking.log_metric[run, 'rmse', 1000.0 / (step + 1), step] done = tracking.end_run[run, 'FINISHED'] Each call answers what it wrote, or why not, and a cell keeps the answer in a name. A value that can fail may not be dropped in Crow, so a failed write stops the cell rather than passing unseen. A notebook cell use myna.tracking (and myna.registry , myna.serving ) and logs with a few calls: Call Does tracking.start_run[experiment, name] Makes the experiment if it is new, starts a run, answers its id tracking.log_params[run, map] , log_param[run, key, value] Records settings; a different value for a key already set is refused tracking.log_metrics[run, map, step] , log_metric[run, key, value, step] Appends values; NaN and infinities are kept as they are tracking.log_input[run, frame, name, context] Records a dataset: digest, schema and row count, from the frame tracking.log_text , log_table , log_artifact Writes a file among the run's artifacts tracking.tag_run[run, key, value] , describe_run[run, text] Tags; the description is the tag mlflow.note.content , as MLflow keeps it tracking.end_run[run, status] FINISHED , FAILED or KILLED , with the end time tracking.history[run, key] , latest_of[run] , runs_in[…] Reads back, for a later cell serving.save_model[run, path, code, …] Writes a model folder ( MLmodel and predict.co ) among the run's artifacts registry.register[run, path, name] Makes the model if it is new and adds a version from the run's folder registry.set_alias[name, alias, version] , transition[…] Aliases and stages serving.evaluate[name, ref, rows, truth, kind, run] Scores a version on rows against the truth, logging each score to the run serving.score[name, ref, body] Asks a version for predictions, as the HTTP endpoint does tests/mlflow/house_prices.co uses every one of them on sample data.

MLflow's HTTP API Myna answers MLflow's own protocol, so mlflow.set_tracking_uri( 'http://localhost:3800') and MLflow's Python client work against it. The client is the test, not an integration Myna depends on. Area Endpoints Experiments ( /api/2.0/mlflow/experiments/… ) create, get, get-by-name, search, update, delete, restore, set-experiment-tag, delete-experiment-tag Runs ( /api/2.0/mlflow/runs/… ) create, get, update, delete, restore, search, log-metric, log-parameter, log-batch, set-tag, delete-tag, log-inputs, outputs; metrics/get-history ; artifacts/list Logged models ( /api/2.0/mlflow/logged-models… ) create, get, finalize, delete, search, set and delete tags Registered models ( /api/2.0/mlflow/registered-models/… ) create, get, rename, update, delete, search, alias (set, delete, get by alias), set-tag, delete-tag, get-latest-versions Model versions ( /api/2.0/mlflow/model-versions/… ) create, get, update, delete, search, get-download-uri, set-tag, delete-tag, transition-stage Traces ( /api/3.0/mlflow/traces… ) start, get, batchGet, search, tags, delete, assessments (create, get, delete) Errors take MLflow's form: {"error_code": "RESOURCE_DOES_NOT_EXIST", "message": …} with status 404, RESOURCE_ALREADY_EXISTS and INVALID_PARAMETER_VALUE with 400.

Serving and Evaluation A model is a folder of files. Its MLmodel file, in MLflow's format, names the flavor crow and the input and output columns. Beside it, predict.co holds fn predict[rows] , which answers one prediction per row, plus whatever files the model reads (its weights). Serving. POST /serve/:model/:ref/invocations takes a version number, an alias or @alias as :ref . The body may be any of MLflow's input forms: dataframe_split , dataframe_records , instances or inputs . The answer is {"predictions": […]} . The model runs by the crow on the PATH, interpreted, in a scratch copy of its folder ( .serving/<id> ) and under a time limit. So a slow or failing model cannot stop the workbench, and a model cannot write into its own folder. Bad input gets a 400 with the reason. Evaluation. serving.evaluate asks the model about the rows and scores what it answers against the truth, with scikit-learn's definitions: For a regressor: mean squared error, root mean squared error, mean absolute error, R² (1 for a perfect fit when the truth does not vary, 0 otherwise), max error, and mean absolute percentage error. For a binary classifier, with 1 as the positive class: accuracy, precision, recall and F1, each 0 where its denominator is 0. Each score is logged as a metric on the run named.

t: MLflow's Known Bugs, and How Myna Avoids Them
x: MLflow's Known Bugs, and How Myna Avoids Them MLflow's issue tracker was read for bugs in the parts Myna rebuilds, and the ones that apply are held off by design: Zero is a value. A step or a time of 0 is kept, not read as missing. NaN. NaN is stored and shown as NaN. It fails every comparison and sorts last. History. The history of a key never logged is an empty list, in step-then-time order. The latest metric is the one at the greatest step, not the last row written. Search is parsed, never pasted into a query. Numbers compare as numbers. Operators may be in any case, either quote mark may be used, and backticked keys are read. Paging has one stable order with the id last, so no run is seen twice or skipped. A bad page token or IS NULL is refused with INVALID_PARAMETER_VALUE . Names. An experiment's name, deleted or not, stays taken. Default (id 0) is made once. Renames. A run's rename changes its name and its mlflow.runName tag only. A registered model's rename moves its tags, aliases and versions. Deleted versions. Deleting a version removes its aliases. Stages. archive_existing_versions archives every other version in the stage. Files. A path with .. , an absolute path or a backslash is refused. A version's source must lie among its run's files. A missing file answers with the relative path, never the server's. Prompts. A prompt is formatted in one pass, so a value's text is never formatted again. Charts are sorted by x with y fitted to the data, and children stay under their parent at any sort.

Tests ./test.sh runs every part's test blocks, interpreted and then compiled, then the checks against Python ( How Experiments and Models Are Tested ). ./test.sh path/to/crow tests another crow. The tests make and remove a workspace of their own, test_data/ , and refuse to run in myna_data/ : an early version of them, run while a server was up, had removed the workspace it was serving.

t: How Experiments and Models Are Tested
x: How Experiments and Models Are Tested ./test.sh runs every part's test blocks, interpreted and then compiled for the pages. The parts are tracking, search, registry, traces, mlapi, charts, experiments, runs, serving and models. It then runs two checks against Python: tests/mlflow/house_prices.co makes 200 houses (area, rooms and age, giving a price with a fixed noise), holding every fifth one out. It fits a linear model by gradient descent at three learning rates, one run each, logging the error at every epoch. It saves each run's model with its weights written into predict.co . It registers the best run as house-price with the alias champion , evaluates it on the held-out rows, and asks the served model for three predictions. tests/mlflow/house_prices.py trains the same model in plain Python loops, adding in the same order. It checks every number the Crow run prints: the centres and spreads, every run's weights and final error, and the three served predictions, all exactly; scikit-learn's six scores to 1e-12, since numpy adds in another order. It runs once interpreted and once compiled. It needs Python with scikit-learn ( ~/.venvs/mlflow , or MYNA_PYTHON ). tests/mlflow/client_check.py drives MLflow's own Python client ( pip install mlflow ) against a running Myna through 25 checks: experiments, runs, params and metric history, tags and search; artifacts, and a scikit-learn model logged as files; the registry with versions, aliases, stages and tags; deletes and restores. Run Myna on a scratch MYNA_DATA first.

The Code Myna is a Crow program of parts, laid out as Magpie's repository is. File What it does main.co Serves the pages myna/workspace.co Reads and writes the logs myna/tally.co A table's size and its columns, read off its files and never off its rows myna/engine.co Makes a notebook into one program, runs it, and reads its output back cell by cell myna/workbench.co The frame every page shares: the sidebar, the top bar and the search myna/queries.co Runs a query, writes it as a cell's Crow, and says it in a line; the dashboards read saved queries through it myna/tiles.co Refreshes a dashboard's tiles and says when one is due myna/tracking.co The experiments' store: runs, params, metrics, tags, datasets, files myna/registry.co Registered models, versions, aliases, stages and prompts myna/search.co MLflow's search grammar, parsed myna/traces.co Traces, spans and feedback myna/serving.co A model's folder, serving and evaluation myna/mlapi.co MLflow's HTTP API over the store, the registry, the search and the traces myna/charts.co The experiments' charts, as SVG myna/notebooks.co , query.co , catalog.co , dashboards.co , jobs.co , settings.co The workbench's pages myna/experiments.co , runs.co , models.co The experiments' and models' pages myna/soon.co The page not built yet scheduler.co The scheduler Nothing in Myna changes Crow's compiler. A bug Myna met in Crow was fixed in Crow, with its test, before Myna went on: 31 of them so far, in three of Crow's commits (f448e81, ce4683d and 8a96a3a).

Not Built Everything is built in Crow, with no integration with an outside framework. These parts of MLflow are left out for that reason: MLflow feature Why not What Myna has Python flavors (scikit-learn, PyTorch, TensorFlow, XGBoost, transformers, …) and serving them Each is a Python framework The crow flavor; MLflow's client can still store any model's files as artifacts Autologging It patches Python libraries Explicit log_* calls Cloud artifact stores (S3, Azure, GCS, HDFS) Outside services The workspace folder SQL tracking backends Magpie is the store Magpie logs Databricks, Unity Catalog, the permissions plugin Outside platform Myna's workspace AI Gateway, deployments to SageMaker, Azure ML, Ray Outside services Myna's own serving Docker images, conda and virtualenv environments Python packaging A model folder run by crow GenAI judges ( mlflow.genai scorers) They call outside models Evaluation's scores, and feedback on traces OpenTelemetry trace export and import ( /v1/traces , protobuf) Outside protocol Traces kept in Myna, spans as JSON Signature inference from Python types Python The columns written in MLmodel Recipes Retired in MLflow Notebooks and jobs And these are not built yet, though they are Crow work: The artifact proxy ( /api/2.0/mlflow-artifacts/… upload and download). MLflow's client writes and reads the workspace's files directly, which works when it runs on the same machine. A client elsewhere needs the proxy. Projects ( MLproject entry points run as jobs). Classifier extras: log loss, the confusion matrix, and a table of every scored row ( eval_results ). On the pages: previews of images and tables among the artifacts; a value shown on hover over a chart; a diff between two prompt versions; downloading a file. Serving speed. A served model is started for each request rather than kept warm: about a second for each call. A logged-model record for a saved model. serving.save_model writes the model's files among the run's artifacts, and a run's page lists them under Artifacts. It makes no logged-model record, as MLflow 3's log_model does, so the run's Logged models card stays empty. MLflow's client's own log_model does make one. Interpreted ( crow run -i main.co ), the Experiments pages answer a click in 9 to 17 seconds once a few sessions are open. Each refresh derives every open page again from the logs. Compiled ( crow run main.co , the default), the same click answers in under 0.1 seconds.

Licensing Myna is source-available under the Business Source License 1.1 (BSL), with an additional use grant. This page says what that means in plain words; where the two differ, the license decides. Free, for everyone Reading, changing and sharing the code. Development, testing, evaluation, continuous integration, staging and demos, on any number of machines. Non-commercial use in production, without limit : an individual's study, research and hobby projects, and charities, schools, public research and government. Commercial use in production on one machine per application : the workspace an application's Myna writes and reads is stored on, and opened from, one machine. Needs a commercial license A company's production use of one application on more than one machine : a workspace on shared or network storage opened by Myna on several machines, or one application's workspace split across machines. Offering Myna, or a product whose main value is Myna, to others as a hosted or managed service . Counting machines A machine is one physical computer or one virtual machine, with every process and container on it. A second machine (needs a license) Not a second machine (free) Myna on another machine opening the same workspace The browsers that open Myna's pages One application's workspace split across machines MLflow's client, or any program, reaching Myna over HTTP A workspace on network storage, opened from several machines Backups of the workspace at rest Restoring onto a replacement machine after a failure The scheduler, the notebooks' runs and served models: processes on the one machine Forks A modified copy stays under the same license, whoever modified it and whatever was added: it may not be used in production beyond these terms, nor offered as a hosted service, and it may not use the name Myna.
